issues.display_title: Issue #1412: Create Collapsible File Manager Sidebar
issues.main_description_html:
Description

To optimize the workspace area, the File Manager sidebar needs a collapsible state. By default, the sidebar should start in a "folded" (minimized) state.

Sub-tasks

  • Toggle Button: Add a fold/expand icon button (e.g. chevron or hamburger menu) at the top or bottom of the sidebar.
  • Default State: Set the initial load state of the sidebar to be collapsed/smaller.
  • Collapsed UI: When folded, hide all folder text labels and reduce the size of the folder icons.
  • Hover State: Implement tooltips. When the sidebar is collapsed and a user hovers over a mini folder icon, display a tooltip showing the folder's name.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. User can smoothly toggle the sidebar between expanded and collapsed states.
  2. The app remembers or defaults to the collapsed state upon initial load.
  3. Folder names are easily discoverable via hover tooltips when in the collapsed state.

RESULT

issues.display_title: Issue #1414: Create Video Menu In Preview Layout
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Design and add a Video Menu to the Preview layout — the on-canvas control surface shown when the previewed source is a 360° video. This is the UI/design counterpart to the engine work in #1410 (360 video support in the new Three.js viewer): #1410 wires up VideoTexture + playback; this task delivers the menu/controls layout users interact with.

Origin (feedback)

From the team chat (GoThru Photo Studio):

albug: "Can it support 360 video also?" anurdin: "yes sure this is support for video also, do you want to add it?" albug: "Yes, I think we should add support for 360 videos" anurdin: "ok Alin noted"

The new viewer was improved in three.js (not Rust) and is faster — video playback is now feasible, so it needs a proper control menu in the Preview layout.

Context / Reference

Grounded in docs/feedback 05-06-2026/analyze-new.md:

  • §3 (Feature Inventory): the File Manager & Preview module hosts the 360° interactive viewer (Three.js / React Three Fiber). This adds the video-control menu to that Preview surface.
  • §4 (funnel): richer Preview deepens the Import → Preview → Publish path before users commit to publishing.
  • §7 (roadmap): the viewer is core daily-driver surface; the video menu must match the "fast, clean viewer" quality bar.

Sub-tasks

  • Video controls bar: Design and overlay a controls bar on the 360 Preview canvas — Play/Pause, timeline/scrubber with current-time & duration, volume control, and full-screen toggle.
  • Conditional display: Show the Video Menu only when the source is a video; for still 360° images keep the existing Preview UI unchanged.
  • Auto-hide / hover behavior: Controls appear on hover / pointer-move and fade out during playback so they don't obstruct the panorama; remain keyboard-accessible.
  • Loading/buffering affordance: Show a buffering indicator (spinner) state in the layout while the video fetches data.
  • Visual consistency: Match the existing HeroUI / Tailwind design language, icons, and theming (light/dark) used elsewhere in Preview.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. When previewing a 360° video, a clean Video Menu appears over the canvas with Play/Pause, scrubber, volume, and full-screen controls.
  2. The menu only shows for video sources; still-image Preview is visually unchanged.
  3. Controls auto-hide during playback and reappear on hover/interaction, without blocking the 360 view.
  4. A buffering/loading state is represented in the layout.
  5. Styling is consistent with the app's existing design system (HeroUI/Tailwind, light & dark themes).

Related

  • Engine / functionality: #1410 — Implement 360 Video Support in New Three.js Viewer.

RESULT

issues.display_title: Issue #1420: Create New Edit Feature AI Image to Video
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Create a new Edit feature: AI Image to Video. Users capture frames from 360°/panorama images, optionally describe each frame (manually or via AI), configure video settings, and generate an AI-produced video from the frame sequence — previewable in the viewer.

UI Reference (from design)

The Edit → AI Image to Video panel shows (per the provided mockup):

  • Header: AI Image to Video, Status (e.g. Success), Output path + Browse, and Remove / View buttons.
  • Video Orientation toggle row: 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16.
  • Main canvas: image/frame viewer.
  • Right Settings panel: Start Frame / End Frame thumbnails, API Key (Select AI Model), Field of View, Camera Angle, Camera Movement dropdowns.

Note: the spec below (Video Settings / Frame Settings / flow) is the source of truth for fields; reconcile with the mockup during design (e.g. Aspect Ratio vs. the Video Orientation toggles; Quality/Pacing/Transition dropdowns).

Video Settings

  • AI API Key (select AI model / key)
  • Aspect Ratio dropdown — 9:16, 16:9
  • Quality dropdown — 720p, 1080p
  • Camera Movement dropdown — straight walkthrough, push in
  • Pacing dropdown — dynamic, continuous
  • Transition dropdown — seamless, morph

Frame Settings

  • Description (per-frame text input)
  • Generate description (AI auto-fill button)

User Flow

  1. Click tab Add Frame.
  2. Select image.
  3. Adjust the image viewer, then click Capture Frame button.
  4. Redirect to the Frame Queue list tab.
  5. Click expand frame → insert a description, or click the AI Generate button → description auto-filled by AI.
  6. Click tab Add Frame to show the empty drag-and-drop image selector, then add an image (same as step 2).
  7. Click tab View Frame to show the frame queue.
  8. Click Settings, then set: AI API Key, Aspect Ratio, Quality, Camera Movement, Pacing, Transition.
  9. Click Generate button → show a toast message + a View button at the viewer.
  10. Click View button → redirect to Preview mode, then show the video player.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. User can add multiple frames by selecting an image, adjusting the viewer, and capturing a frame; captured frames appear in the Frame Queue.
  2. Each frame supports a manual description and an AI Generate description action that auto-fills the field.
  3. The Settings panel exposes all Video Settings (API key, aspect ratio, quality, camera movement, pacing, transition) with the specified options, and persists the selections for the generate request.
  4. Clicking Generate triggers the AI video generation, shows a toast, and surfaces a View button on completion.
  5. Clicking View opens Preview mode with a working video player of the generated result.
  6. Tabs (Add Frame, Frame Queue / View Frame, Settings), Output/Browse, Remove, and Video Orientation behave per the design; styling consistent with the existing design system (HeroUI/Tailwind, light & dark).

Open points to confirm in design

  • Aspect Ratio dropdown (9:16, 16:9) vs. the mockup's Video Orientation toggles (16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16) — which is authoritative / do both exist?
  • Mockup also shows Field of View and Camera Angle dropdowns not in the settings list above — include them?
  • Which AI provider(s) back the generation (Gemini / OpenAI) and how the API key maps to "Select AI Model".

RESULT

issues.display_title: Issue #1422: Create New Edit Feature Scale Up Image
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Create a new Edit feature: Scale Up Image — let users enlarge (upscale) images by a quality multiplier. The layout is almost the same as Batch Image Resize, but oriented around file size and a quality multiplier instead of width/resize dimensions.

Update (spec revision):

  • "Resize" / "Resized" → "File Size".
  • Per-file row shows only the file size (e.g. 8 MB) — no "Current: …" secondary value.
  • "Width" input → "Quality" dropdown with options 2x, 3x, 4x.
  • Overall layout almost identical to the Batch Image Resize reference.

UI Reference (based on Batch Image Resize layout)

Reuse the Batch Image Resize layout, adapted:

  • Queue header with counts: Total / Queue / Success / Failed / Canceled, plus Remove All and Add to Queue buttons.
  • Output path field + Browse button.
  • Per-file table: File Name, File Size (single value, e.g. 8 MB), Status (Queued), Action (remove ✕).
  • Right Settings panel: a quality-loss note ("Enlarging an image beyond its original size will reduce its quality."), a Save as New File toggle, a Quality dropdown (2x / 3x / 4x), and a green Scale Up button with the note "These settings will be applied to all items in the queue."

Scope

Scale Up reuses the Batch Image Resize flow but is oriented toward enlarging:

  • Pick a Quality multiplier (2x / 3x / 4x) applied to all queued items.
  • Batch queue of multiple images, each row showing its file size (single value) and per-item status.
  • Save as New File toggle (avoid overwriting source).
  • Output directory selection (Browse).
  • Quality-loss warning when enlarging beyond original size.

Sub-tasks

  • Scale Up panel: Build the Edit → Scale Up panel based on the Batch Image Resize layout (Queue, Output + Browse, per-file table, Settings).
  • Quality multiplier: Replace the Width input with a Quality dropdown offering 2x / 3x / 4x, applied to all queued items.
  • File size column: Per-file table shows the File Size only (e.g. 8 MB) — no "Current" dimension/size line.
  • Batch queue: Add to Queue / Remove All / per-item remove; statuses (Queued → Processing → Success/Failed/Canceled) with live counts.
  • Save as New File toggle + Output: honor the toggle and the selected output directory.
  • Quality warning: show the "enlarging reduces quality" note.
  • Run scale up: the Scale Up button applies the selected multiplier to all queued items and processes them.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. User can add multiple images to the queue and select a Quality multiplier (2x / 3x / 4x) applied to all items.
  2. Each queued item shows its file size (single value) and an accurate status; counts update during processing.
  3. Save as New File and Output/Browse work; outputs land in the chosen location without overwriting source when the toggle is on.
  4. The quality-loss warning is shown.
  5. Clicking Scale Up upscales all queued items by the chosen multiplier; success/failure is reported per item; queue controls (Remove All, per-item remove) work.
  6. Layout/behavior consistent with the existing Batch Image Resize design (HeroUI/Tailwind, light & dark).

Open points to confirm in design

  • "Quality (as a percentage)" vs. the dropdown options 2x / 3x / 4x — the options are multipliers, not percentages; confirm the intended label/semantics.
  • Is Scale Up a distinct feature or a mode/variant of Batch Image Resize?
  • Upscaling engine: simple resample (sharp) vs. an AI super-resolution upscaler — 2x/3x/4x multipliers suggest a super-resolution approach; confirm which.

RESULT
